title: Travel and transport
objectives: I can buy a bus or plane ticket and ask about schedules, platforms and gates.
I can book a room in a hotel or pousada and ask what is included.
I can choose the right preposition for transport (de ônibus, a pé) and destinations (ir a, ir para, estar em).
I can make polite requests with eu queria and eu gostaria de.
I can describe a past trip combining the preterite and the imperfect.

grammar.title: Prepositions with transport and destinations
grammar.explanation:
To say how you travel, Portuguese uses de plus the vehicle: de ônibus, de avião, de carro, de trem, de metrô, de táxi, de bicicleta, de Uber. On foot is the exception, a pé. Compare Vou de ônibus (I go by bus) with Estou no ônibus (I am on the bus): de names the means, while em (no, na) says where you physically are.

For destinations, ir takes a or para. A is more formal and used for short visits: Vou ao mercado, Vou à praia. Para suggests a longer stay or a trip, and in speech para is pronounced pra: Vou pra Bahia, Ele foi pro Rio. Chegar uses a or em, and em is extremely common in Brazil: Cheguei em São Paulo, Chegamos ao hotel.

For location, use em: Moro em Recife, Estou em casa, Fiquei no hotel. Remember the special cases: casa and trabalho take no article in Vou pra casa and Estou em casa, but Vou ao trabalho and Estou no trabalho. Contractions are automatic: a + o = ao, a + a = à, em + o = no, em + a = na, para + o = pro (speech), para + a = pra.

grammar.title: Polite requests: eu queria and eu gostaria de
grammar.explanation:
When you ask for something from a clerk, a hotel receptionist or a stranger, Brazilians rarely use the plain present quero, which can sound abrupt. The usual polite forms are Eu queria, which is the imperfect of querer used to soften the request, and Eu gostaria de, the conditional of gostar de, which is a little more formal. Both are followed by a noun or by an infinitive: Eu queria uma passagem, Eu gostaria de reservar um quarto.

To ask someone to do something, use Você poderia plus an infinitive (Você poderia me ajudar?) or the simpler Pode plus an infinitive (Pode me dizer onde fica o portão?). Adding por favor, com licença or desculpa is normal. Remember that gostaria needs de before an infinitive or a noun, but queria does not: Eu queria uma passagem, Eu gostaria de uma passagem.

In service situations, you will also hear Me vê plus noun in shops (Me vê um café) and Vou querer, which is the near future with ir: Vou querer um café. These are casual and are common in restaurants and snack bars.

grammar.title: Schedules and duration: sai às, chega às, demora
grammar.explanation:
Schedules use the present tense in Portuguese: O ônibus sai às oito e chega às duas. For the time you use à, às, ao meio-dia (noon) and à meia-noite (midnight). To ask what time, say A que horas sai o ônibus? or, more casually, Que horas o ônibus sai? The next and last services are o próximo ônibus and o último ônibus.

To say how long a trip takes, use demorar or levar: A viagem demora seis horas, Leva três horas de carro. Ask with Quanto tempo demora? or Quanto tempo leva? Add de ônibus, de avião and so on to specify the means.

Other useful schedule phrases are a partir de (starting from), até (until), de hora em hora (every hour), a cada vinte minutos (every twenty minutes), cedo (early) and tarde (late). For the check-in and check-out of a hotel you say O check-in é a partir das duas e o check-out é até o meio-dia. The delayed flight is o voo atrasado and the flight on time is no horário.

grammar.title: Narrating a trip: preterite and imperfect together
grammar.explanation:
A travel story mixes both past tenses. Events in sequence are in the preterite: Chegamos, deixamos as malas, fomos à praia. Descriptions, feelings and background go in the imperfect: Era noite, fazia frio, a pousada era pequena, a dona era simpática. When something was in progress and was interrupted, the progressive helps: Estávamos esperando o ônibus quando começou a chover.

Connectors keep the story moving: primeiro, depois, em seguida, mais tarde, no dia seguinte, por fim. Add time markers such as no ano passado, há dois anos, no verão passado. To give opinions, use adjectives in the imperfect for description: A comida era deliciosa, O quarto era limpo.

Also review the irregular verbs you need in trips: fui, fomos (ir), fiz, fizemos (fazer), vi, vimos (ver), tive (ter), estive (estar) and trouxe (trazer). A nice closing line is Foi uma viagem incrível. The verb ser in this closing comment is in the preterite because it evaluates the whole trip as a finished event.

culture.title: Getting around Brazil
culture.text:
Brazil is huge, so how you travel depends a lot on the distance. For long distances many people fly, and the main domestic airlines sell cheap tickets in installments called parcelado. For medium distances and for budget travel, buses are the backbone of the country. Every city has a rodoviária, often a bustling building with ticket counters called guichês. Buses come in different classes: convencional, executivo and leito, a sleeper with reclining seats that is comfortable for overnight trips.

Inside large cities, the metrô is the fastest option in São Paulo, Rio, Belo Horizonte, Recife, Salvador and Brasília, but it covers only part of the city. Buses are everywhere and the ticket is often paid with an electronic card or Pix. Apps like Uber and 99 are very popular, often cheaper than a táxi, and people say Vou de Uber as naturally as Vou de ônibus. If a friend has a car, pedir carona (asking for a ride) is a common and friendly habit.

For accommodation, besides hotels and hostels you will find pousadas, small guesthouses that often include café da manhã in the rate and are usually run by a family. The best-known destinations include the Cristo Redentor and Pão de Açúcar in Rio, the beaches of Bahia and Pernambuco, the Pantanal, the Amazon, Foz do Iguaçu, Fernando de Noronha and the colonial towns of Minas Gerais such as Ouro Preto. Asking locals for dicas (tips) is the best way to find a good restaurant or a hidden beach.

paragraphs.pt: No ano passado, eu e minha irmã viajamos de ônibus para Ouro Preto. A viagem demorou oito horas e o ônibus chegou atrasado. Era noite e fazia muito frio.
paragraphs.en: Last year, my sister and I traveled by bus to Ouro Preto. The trip took eight hours and the bus arrived late. It was night and very cold.

paragraphs.pt: Ficamos numa pousada pequena perto do centro. O café da manhã era incluído e a dona, Dona Cida, era muito simpática. Ela nos deu um mapa e explicou os melhores passeios.
paragraphs.en: We stayed at a small guesthouse near the center. Breakfast was included and the owner, Dona Cida, was very friendly. She gave us a map and explained the best tours.

paragraphs.pt: No dia seguinte, fomos a pé até a igreja e tiramos muitas fotos. Por fim, voltamos pra casa de ônibus. Estávamos cansadas, mas felizes.
paragraphs.en: The next day, we walked to the church and took many photos. Finally, we went home by bus. We were tired, but happy.
